_comment: Copy to <run>/deliverables/report_sections.json. These are the prose
sections the reviewer authors; everything else in the report is assembled
from the canonical evidence by report_model.py.
This file REPLACES build_pdf.py's --intro-file / --methods-file /
--conclusions-file / --next-steps-file arguments. Those four loose files went
to the PDF only, and build_review.py had no way to receive them at all, so
review.md shipped with no Introduction, Methods, Conclusions or Next steps
while the PDF had all four. They still work as a fallback when this file is
absent, so existing runs keep building.
THE RULE, identical to claim_narratives.jsonl: every statement must EITHER
cite evidence_ids that exist in evidence/evidence.jsonl, OR set
"inference": true, in which case it renders under an explicit
reviewer-inference label in both deliverables. A statement with neither is a
contract violation and both builders refuse to render. Methods and Next steps
are normally the reviewer's own words and are flagged as such: an un-cited
sentence in the Conclusions is exactly as unattributable as an un-cited
sentence under a claim.
CONCLUSIONS have an additional consistency contract. Every evidence-based
conclusion lists claim_ids, and every listed claim must contribute at least
one of the statement's evidence_ids. If all cited rows are secondary or
indirect, word the conclusion accordingly and set qualified=true; the report
then prints a secondary/indirect-evidence marker.
Each section is a list of statements rendered in order — as paragraphs for
introduction/methods/conclusions, and as a numbered list for next_steps.
A bare list is accepted in place of {"statements": [...]}. Omit a section
you have nothing for; the report then prints an explicit not-supplied note
under the heading rather than an empty section.
THREE SECTIONS BEHAVE DIFFERENTLY.
key_findings renders in the SUMMARY, directly under Table 1. Every item
must cite retained evidence_ids. Do not put grounded executive-summary
findings under external_findings merely because they are important.
external_findings renders in the SUMMARY, right under Table 1, not as its own
heading. Put a result here when it bears on the conclusion but has no
retrievable full text — a conference abstract, a trial registry entry, an
announcement. A shipped review's single most decision-relevant fact (its
phase 3 trial missing the primary endpoint) reached the reader two thirds of
the way through Conclusions as an unattributed "[reviewer inference]",
because it could not be grounded. An honest gap in grounding must change how
a finding is LABELLED, not where it sits.
limitations is APPENDED to measured facts the builders emit themselves —
full texts obtained vs selected, claims dropped, figures shown vs considered,
claims on weak tiers. Write only what those numbers do not already say.

statements.text: REPLACE with the decision the review informs and why the question is open.
REPLACE with the state of the field as the retrieved papers report it.
REPLACE with the search: sources queried, date window, and inclusion rule.
REPLACE with how evidence was accepted: verbatim quote plus resolvable locator per claim, support tiers derived from the accepted rows rather than asserted.
REPLACE, or omit. State the most decision-relevant result that is grounded in retained full text.

REPLACE, or omit this section. Example: the phase 3 trial of X in Y did not meet its primary clinical endpoint; reported at conference level, so no full text was retrievable and no verbatim anchor exists.
REPLACE with the bottom line the evidence supports, hedged to the weakest support tier it rests on.
REPLACE with what follows for the decision, which no single source states.

REPLACE, or omit. The builders already state the retrieval shortfall, dropped claims, figures passed over and weak-tier claims; add only what those numbers do not say (e.g. a named foundational paper that was not retrievable and which claim it would upgrade).
REPLACE with the experiment or retrieval that would close the largest evidence gap.
REPLACE with the contradiction worth adjudicating first, and how.
